newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram draws flak over petrol comment.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram draws flak over petrol comment.

text.p: Partners of India's coalition government sharply criticised Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Tuesday for saying the government was considering raising the prices of petroleum products.

"Who has given him the right to speak on behalf of the Left parties?" United News of India (UNI) quoted Communist Party of India (CPI) leader Gurudas Dasgupta as telling the upper house of parliament.
The CPI is part of Prime Minster H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party minority coalition.
Chidambaram was quoted on Sunday as saying the government was considering raising petroleum prices to cover the burgeoning cost of petrol subsidies.

His comments sparked a storm of protest among left-wing parties, which fear price rises will hit the working class. Communists strongly criticised the government when it raised petroleum prices shortly after taking power in June.

S.B. Chavan of the Congress party, which provides crucial parliamentary support to Deve Gowda's government, said Chidambaram's statement was at odds with parliamentary rules and "like leaking the budget proposals".
"We will like to know from the minister what were the compelling circumstances in which he made the announcement," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Chavan as saying.
Members of the Communist Party of India-Marxist, which supports Deve Gowda's government without being part of the cabinet, also criticised Chidambaram, who was in Japan on an official visit.

Chidambaram was quoted on Sunday by PTI as saying the previous government of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, which was turned out of power following general elections in April and May, had made the mistake of not raising petroleum prices.
The finance minister said Gowda's United Front coalition government had taken the "courageous step" of raising petroleum prices shortly after taking power in June.
But the Petroleum Ministry said last week that there was no plan for an immediate increase in petroleum prices.
Ministry officials estimate that the oil pool deficit is expected to touch 155 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) against 57 billion rupees last year.
